[[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXU-Vl9fuC3KKF2mIwSVy9i_iLcRGyubOIqe8g637bYoKdJHAQwrK4vMVa61I-QO9lLiyB9s8_SELH0ofNiR4ZIZFfGaRlUNVXA7WcOrJ8I1O3QYpKj_Laai-1bMaiEA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF121n_gMlFWYiSjkGoojDLT6G4seixT10BcEzfD__LKiMl7fpjaErPYp21ctT_TEH5LI5_6MRh60r9gMNVuGAANuQgQeTchU4BBpVpr8cbTNm9BfCcqUPQIw_qG1tcLM7SA1W0qQTyS3wqpoW9xSk_P-GiEv9OmhZNOY9bA)]
Key Concepts

* The Synoptic Problem: The Q source helps explain why Matthew and Luke share roughly 235 verses of material (mostly sayings, parables, and teachings like the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer) that do not appear in the [Gospel of Mark](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXugowpqVJsFBq_iAYJQTmbaROqWgTiR3teG-8LJfYDHc5fNLv64E80RaFD3UC4OTPihiVbbNqxRHD1ur9MndSFXkUaGh6o6eE2AiZK563iUaYe4qpurVvu8MoM6TjdJcJLr-wZH41uBaeEKIvfnUD5wqf9zct). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXX8bntLFbhlFJ0VjtIRbW1Ro5x4mQHmjC4t_5fO_Guj8pg4PAVkDuS7KUqsXlMHtpXKxBWdU7ul_s9P1i8Zh-RZfpycTnDqkm6r78xtbjO-2aNCSUYGTqLAFa0CunzLI_OuOsH_2owtO1W), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF121n_gMlFWYiSjkGoojDLT6G4seixT10BcEzfD__LKiMl7fpjaErPYp21ctT_TEH5LI5_6MRh60r9gMNVuGAANuQgQeTchU4BBpVpr8cbTNm9BfCcqUPQIw_qG1tcLM7SA1W0qQTyS3wqpoW9xSk_P-GiEv9OmhZNOY9bA)]
* The Two-Source Hypothesis: This major scholarly model argues that both Matthew and Luke wrote independently of one another, utilizing two primary documents: the Gospel of Mark (for narrative structure) and Q (for shared teachings). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXU-Vl9fuC3KKF2mIwSVy9i_iLcRGyubOIqe8g637bYoKdJHAQwrK4vMVa61I-QO9lLiyB9s8_SELH0ofNiR4ZIZFfGaRlUNVXA7WcOrJ8I1O3QYpKj_Laai-1bMaiEA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF121n_gMlFWYiSjkGoojDLT6G4seixT10BcEzfD__LKiMl7fpjaErPYp21ctT_TEH5LI5_6MRh60r9gMNVuGAANuQgQeTchU4BBpVpr8cbTNm9BfCcqUPQIw_qG1tcLM7SA1W0qQTyS3wqpoW9xSk_P-GiEv9OmhZNOY9bA)]

findings: THE ONE FACT ABOUT Q FILED AS AN ALTERNATIVE. 'No physical or ancient manuscripts of Q have ever been discovered.' The sentence closes the 'Alternative Theories' item, after Farrer. It states the evidentiary condition of the hypothesis, and the composition places it as a feature of the minority position.

EVIDENCE FROM EXTANT TEXTS, CREDITED TO AN UNATTESTED ONE. The 'Supporting Evidence' is the wording shared by Matthew and Luke ('implying they relied on a common written tradition rather than copying one another') and an extant genre ('The 1945 discovery of the Nag Hammadi library (including the Gospel of Thomas) proved that standalone sayings collections did circulate in early Christianity.'). The first is a relation between two extant gospels, explained by Q only once direct dependence is excluded, and the composition gives the exclusion as an implication. The second shows that sayings collections existed; it is evidence for the genre, and Thomas is extant.

THE ARCHIVE'S DISTINCTION, ABSENT. The archive's position holds the classes apart and reports 'Quelle A and Q' as reconstructed antecedents (#1741 §11.7).
